downloadedSourceCountNote: Zero, and here zero is the finding rather than a policy constraint. The download could not be performed because none of the three identities names a file that any official body publishes. The documents actually inspected — the current Florida Bar rules compilation and a superseded compilation still live on the Court's own media host — were retrieved into temporary storage outside the repository and discarded. Nothing entered version control, no materialization destination was written and no receipt was created.

controllingIntegratedDecisions.carriedForward: Rule 3.989 prescribes four forms and publishes them as text inside the rule; the Florida courts publish no fillable PDF of any of them. The Court's own Court Forms page lists eleven PDFs and none is an expunction or sealing form.

Subdivision (a) is the Sworn Statement, retitled from Affidavit by SC19-1983 effective 2019-12-19; the affidavit role is retainable on all three affidavit components, and fl-trafficking-affidavit-2 is bound to the wrong rule and belongs under Rule 3.9895(b).

method.description: Attempted public official download of three Rule 3.989 identities, followed by independent re-verification of the controlling publication. The two integrated Florida decisions were treated as controlling and were not reopened; what this job adds is the acquisition attempt itself, a fresh digest comparison on the controlling compilation, the four printed form captions read from the current text, a complete reading of the compilation's amendment table to its final row, and a digest for the legacy trap that no prior job recorded.
method.tooling: curl for retrieval and HTTP status; sha256 and byte counts on retrieved bytes; poppler (pdfinfo, pdftotext -layout) for structure, rule spans and amendment-table reads
method.assignmentConstraintObserved: The stop condition requires using only the assigned public official sources, recording provenance and hashes, stopping if identity, revision or issuer authority is uncertain, and not altering legal conclusions. Identity, revision and issuer are all certain for the rule; what is absent is a file. No legal conclusion is altered — the two integrated Florida decisions are carried forward, not revisited.

finding.headline: The assignment is a download job for three documents that are not published as files. Rule 3.989's four forms exist as text printed inside the rule, and no official Florida body publishes a standalone binary for any of them. The correct result is not an acquisition failure but a statement that the acquisition premise is wrong: there is nothing to download, and there never was.
finding.acquisitionRequiredRationale: No issuer interaction can produce a file the Supreme Court of Florida does not publish. The three queue rows should not remain open download jobs.
finding.whyThisIsNotAStopCondition: The stop condition directs stopping where identity, revision or issuer authority is uncertain. None of the three is uncertain here. The rule's caption, its effective date, its promulgating court and its four printed form captions are all established from the current official text. Stopping would withhold a settled answer.

checksCarriedForwardFromTheIntegratedDec: The Florida Courts Help expunge-and-seal page returns HTTP 200 with a soft-404 body reading that the requested page cannot be found, and has no archive snapshots.
The flcourts.gov form-database query for 'expunge' returns HTTP 200 with zero form results.
An Internet Archive CDX enumeration of flcourts.gov and flcourts-media.flcourts.gov filtered to URLs containing 'expunge' returns empty.

The Supreme Court's own Court Forms page lists eleven PDFs — name change, emeritus lawyer package, notice to invoke, civil indigency, in forma pauperis, jurisdiction brief template, AOSC13-7, the IOP manual, the Bar and UPL referee manuals and the strategic plan. No expunction or sealing form.
flcourtsPublishesNoExpunctionForm.negativeIsAffirmative: Four independent checks across two official hosts, including an archive enumeration that would have caught a withdrawn page. This is a proven absence, not a failed search.

commercialUseAndLicensing.theCourtsOwnText: Florida court rules are the Supreme Court of Florida's own promulgated text. No licence or reuse statement was located on flcourts.gov governing it.
commercialUseAndLicensing.theBarCompilation: The Florida Bar is a private organisation and its compilation is a republication. Any terms it carries govern its compilation, not the Court's underlying rule text, and the two must not be conflated.
commercialUseAndLicensing.queueRecordedPosition: The queue records the publisher's licensing and commercial-use terms as unresolved on all three rows. That remains correct.
commercialUseAndLicensing.doNotInfer: Public availability of a rules compilation is not permission to redistribute a derived form. And because the forms are rule text rather than files, the reuse question here is about reproducing statutory-style text, which is a different question from redistributing a government form file.
commercialUseAndLicensing.notAnswered: No licence question was assigned to this job and none is decided. Escalation is human-only.
commercialUseAndLicensing.consequence: generationAllowed must remain false on all three identities.

doNotSubstitute.document: the January 1, 2017 flcourts-media compilation at sha256 80c82952…0fa039
doNotSubstitute.why: Still live at HTTP 200 on the Court's own media host, larger than the current compilation, and six years stale. It carries the superseded Affidavit title and the pre-carve-out human-trafficking subdivisions.

Human Trafficking: Sworn Statement; Petition; and Order to Expunge or Seal Records. Its forms are near-identical in shape to 3.989's but implement § 943.0583, a different statute and a different relief, and it has been amended since 3.989 was. One assigned component is already known to belong here.

Motion for Postconviction Relief. The one nearby rule carrying additional-pages language, which makes it the top hit for any continuation-style keyword search in the criminal rules. Nothing to do with expunction.

Petition to Seal or Expunge — the procedural rule, cited on the face of both order forms. It contains no forms. Citing it as the source of a form is the same rule-number-as-form-identity error resolved elsewhere in this programme.
FDLE 40-021, 40-025, 40-026 and 40-028 are the agency-stage applications resolved by a separate job now awaiting integration. They precede the court stage and are not Rule 3.989 forms.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest disposition the evidence supports. It is not unresolved_identity: all three resolve to named subdivisions of a rule whose caption, effective date, promulgating court and four printed form captions are established from the current official text. It is not acquisition_blocked: nothing blocked retrieval, and the compilation was retrieved twice at a stable digest. It is not simply identity_established_binary_unavailable, which is what the edition records — that phrasing asserts a file exists and is merely unobtained, and the opposite is true. And it is not a clean three-way resolution either, because the order identity stands for two mutually exclusive forms.
terminalDispositionDetail.newDefectsFoundDetail: FL-RULE-3.989-ORDER stands for both subdivision (b) Order to Expunge and subdivision (c) Order to Seal.

implementationFamilyEffect.effectOfThisJob: Three Florida identities move from open download jobs to a settled negative: the documents are rule text and no file exists to acquire. Eleven components across four tracks stop waiting on a retrieval that can never succeed. A new defect is surfaced — one order identity standing for two mutually exclusive orders — which would have produced an expunction track and a sealing track resolving to the same document. The legacy trap gains a digest, and Rule 3.9895's 2021 amendment is recorded for the first time.
implementationFamilyEffect.familyReadinessStatement: The Florida official-PDF family remains fail-closed and this job does not move it. All four tracks carry outputStrategy official_pdf_fill for instruments that have no PDF at all, which is a design question this lane does not decide. No component is rebound, generation is not permitted, runtime is disabled and no field map is built. No packet becomes generatable and no renderer is assigned.
implementationFamilyEffect.outputStrategyTension: Eleven components are typed official_pdf_fill and there is no official PDF to fill. The same tension was already recorded for the affidavit identity by the integrated decision and for Louisiana elsewhere in this programme. Recorded, not resolved — resolving it is a legal-design decision.

expectedDownstreamEffect: Three Florida acquisition keys close without acquisition, and the reason is recorded as a proven negative rather than a failed retrieval: the Supreme Court of Florida publishes these four forms as text inside Rule 3.989 and no official host serves a standalone file for any of them. Eleven components across four tracks stop depending on an impossible download. One order identity is shown to stand for two mutually exclusive forms — Order to Expunge under § 943.0585 and Order to Seal under § 943.059 — which is a live defect that would have bound an expunction track and a sealing track to the same document. Rule 3.989 is confirmed unamended since 2019-12-19 by a complete reading of the compilation's amendment table to its final row, while Rule 3.9895 is newly recorded as amended on 2021-10-28, which changes the currentness of the trafficking components the integrated decision reassigned to it. The legacy 2017 compilation gains a digest and is shown to be larger than the current one, so size cannot be used as a currency heuristic. No binary is acquired, no receipt is created, nothing enters version control, no rule text is converted into a form, no county packet is substituted, no component is rebound, no memo is edited, no edition is published, no packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.
